questions.prompt: The report suggests that advocates for compulsory voting view the act of casting a ballot as ______
options: A voluntary expression of personal liberty.
A societal requirement on par with fiscal contributions.
A unique privilege distinct from other civic tasks.
A method to ensure the silent majority remains polarized.

questions.prompt: Critics of voting fines suggest that abstention can function as ______
options: A random choice to avoid state coercion.
Evidence of a lack of civic engagement.
A form of voter suppression against the base.
A deliberate non-verbal critique of the ballot options.

questions.prompt: According to the text, the threat of a fine might result in ______
options: Arbitrary candidate selection.
Enhanced freedom of expression.
More qualified candidates entering the race.
A more informed outcome for the silent majority.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the "ethical dilemma" mentioned ______
options: The conflict between state-mandated duty and individual autonomy.
The struggle to define taxation as a fundamental social obligation.
The difficulty of increasing turnout among polarized extremes.
The trade-off between financial penalties and jury service.

questions.prompt: The report implies that a "democratic mandate" is "more accurate" when ______
options: Voters are well-informed and choose at random.
Participation is no longer a choice but a penalty.
The government reflects the breadth of the citizenry.
Personal liberty is prioritized over social obligation.
Eliminates the silent majority.
Invalidates the communicative power of not voting.
Promotes a more powerful democratic mandate.
Protects the sanctity of personal liberty.
